govdocs-archive_org-nsia-BirminghamIndic: This Birmingham indictment fragment — creator unknown — is a legal file. The file’s full context is unclear. Indictments charge crimes in court. Birmingham’s civil-rights era was turbulent. Researchers value such files. The item is a fragment of the legal record.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-BlavatskyFounda: This Blavatsky file — maker unknown — is a net-archive bit on the god-lore founder. Helena B. set up the Wisdom School in 1875. The craze spread far and wide. The file’s whole tale is dark. The bit is a shelf-oddity.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-CIAEngland_CIA_: Christopher Walker’s piece — CIA men in Britain checking on subversion — covers CIA activity in the UK. The file belongs to the intelligence archive. Allies spied on allies in the Cold War. The item is a fragment of press history.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-PublicityEnglan: Robert Pitman’s Sunday Express article — ‘What is the TRUTH about...’ — is a British press piece. The British press chased the story. The headline promised answers. The file belongs to the press archive. The item is a fragment of press history.
the-misuse-of-mind: Psychoanalyst Karin Stephen takes aim at two fashionable ideas of her day: Henri Bergson's philosophy, which distrusted cold reason, and the looser claims of early psychology. With crisp logic she argues that the mind's thinking powers deserve more credit, not less. Published in 1922, the book is a sharp, readable snapshot of the intellectual battles fought as modern psychology was being born.
the-letters-of-norah-on-her-tour-through: Writing simply as Norah, the author tours Ireland and sends home vivid letters describing the towns, countryside, and people she meets. Her fresh eyes capture the Ireland of her day — its beauty, its poverty, its humor. Part travelogue, part personal journal, the letters make an engaging companion for armchair travelers.
history-of-king-charles-the-second-of-en: Jacob Abbott — whose histories taught generations of young Americans — tells the story of the Merry Monarch. From exile to Restoration, Charles II's adventurous reign unfolds in clear, lively chapters for young readers. Abbott had a gift for making history feel like story, and Charles makes a most entertaining subject.
sganarelle-or-the-self-deceived-husband: Molière's brisk one-act comedy turns on Sganarelle, a husband convinced his wife is unfaithful — and wrong about nearly everything. Mistaken identities and quick misunderstandings drive the farce at a breathless pace. An early triumph of the young Molière, it shows his comic machinery already running at full speed.
nets-to-catch-the-wind: Elinor Wylie's first book of poems announced a distinctive new voice — cool, precise, and glittering. Her lyrics on beauty, art, and the natural world are crafted like cut glass. Though her life was brief and stormy, these poems secured her place among the finest American poets of the 1920s.
life-of-harriet-beecher-stowe-compiled-f: Compiled by her son Charles from her letters and journals, this biography lets Harriet Beecher Stowe tell much of her own story. The author of Uncle Tom's Cabin emerges as a devoted mother, a tireless reformer, and a woman of deep faith. An intimate, family-authorized portrait of one of America's most influential writers.
algonquin-legends-of-new-england: Folklorist Charles Godfrey Leland collected these myths and tales from the Algonquin peoples of New England — stories of the culture hero Glooskap, of giants, spirits, and the making of the world. Recorded from living storytellers, the legends preserve a rich Native American tradition. A pioneering work of American folklore.
boy-scouts-of-the-air-on-lost-island: Gordon Stuart's aerial scouts fly to a mysterious lost island in this high-flying adventure. Strange discoveries and narrow escapes await the young aviators far from home. Written when airplanes were still marvels, the story bubbles with the excitement of early flight.
the-battle-ground: Ellen Glasgow's Civil War novel follows a Virginia family through secession, battle, and defeat with rare honesty. Writing as a Southerner, she treats the Confederacy's tragedy without romance or apology. A powerful, clear-eyed classic of Southern literature and one of the finest novels of the war.
the-motor-girls-on-cedar-lake-or-the-her: Margaret Penrose's Motor Girls speed to Cedar Lake, where the hermit of Fern Island guards his lonely mystery. Motoring fun, camp chatter, and girl detective work combine in this lively series tale. A cheerful period adventure for young readers. Sun, speed, and sleuthing fill this bright tale of the motor age's young heroines.
malayan-literature-comprising-romantic-t: Chauncey Starkweather opens the treasure-house of Malayan literature — romantic tales, epic poetry, and royal chronicles from the Malay world. These translations bring a rich, little-known tradition to English readers. A pioneering window onto Southeast Asian letters. Kings, lovers, and heroes people these pages, opening a rich world few Western readers know.
the-strange-cabin-on-catamount-island: Lawrence Leslie's boys' mystery centers on the strange cabin on Catamount Island — who built it, and what secrets does it hide? Young heroes investigate with pluck and curiosity. A fine old-fashioned adventure for boys. Footprints, locked doors, and island secrets keep young readers guessing to the very end.
how-sammy-went-to-coral-land: Emily Paret Atwater's How Sammy Went to Coral-Land takes young readers on a voyage beneath the waves to coral wonders — polyps, fishes, and submarine gardens. Her instructive fancy delights while it teaches natural history. A charming children's undersea tale.
snow-blind: Katharine Newlin Burt's Snow-Blind is a novel of the Wyoming sheep country, where a blizzard blinds more than eyes — passion and pride rage like the storm. Her western romance grips with the force of the weather it names. A strong, stark tale of the high plains.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbey-of-croy: This 1913 Catholic Encyclopedia article on the Abbey of Croyland — the fenland house of St. Guthlac — tells of its marshy origins and medieval wealth. Oswald Hunter-Blair gives its history. A solid reference on an English fen abbey. Guthlac's fen hermitage grew into a mitred abbey.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbey-of-mori: A 1913 piece on Morimond, fourth daughter of Cîteaux. Its sons spread east to Poland and Spain. Edmond Obrecht traces its line. The Cistercian family tree at its root. Its abbots sat as fathers over a hundred daughter houses. Its name means the death of the world.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-absalon-of-lu: This 1913 reference article on Absalon of Lund — Denmark's warrior archbishop and statesman. Thomas Shahan celebrates the founder of Copenhagen. He fought Wends and built churches. A prelate who wielded both cross and sword. Saxo wrote Denmark's history at his command.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ancient-see-o: This 1913 reference article on the ancient see of Ribe — Denmark's oldest bishopric. Arthur Taylor honors its primacy. St. Ansgar preached on its shores. Its cathedral crowns the marsh town. The mother see of Denmark. Its stork nests crown the rooftops.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-antoine-galla: This 1913 reference piece on Antoine Galland — the translator of the Arabian Nights. Pierre Fournet honors his eastern lore. His Scheherazade enchanted Europe. The Academy prized his manuscripts. The man who gave us Aladdin. His diary charms the modern reader. His manuscripts rest in the royal library.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-auckland: This 1913 reference piece on Auckland — the New Zealand diocese. Henry Cleary gives its pioneer story. Its bishops served the settler towns. The Maori missions tested their zeal. A bishopric of the southern seas. Its St. Patrick's crowns the city hill.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-basutoland: This 1913 reference article on Basutoland — the mountain kingdom's missions. Armand Langouet tells its hard story. The priests climbed to the high villages. The Basuto kept their rugged pride. The Church's highland mission. Its pony treks cross the high passes. Its missions dot the Maluti foothills.
